mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline during periods of rising HOUST (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not positive when UNRATE falls below 5% in majority of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payroll employment and a decline in unemployment rate indicates a robust labor market, driving positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between joint labor indicators and SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate above 4.5% tightens monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive despite high FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales growth indicates strong consumer spending, which drives corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Retail sales growth does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: CPI exceeding 240 indicates high inflation, leading to potential rate hikes and negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive despite high CPI (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production alongside retail sales indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between industrial production growth and SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment may not prevent market decline as other factors dominate.
failure_condition: Low UNRATE in late-cycle does not lead to positive SPX returns (t-test p > 0.05).
